newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Housing Bank boosts bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Housing Bank boosts bourse trade.

text.p: Jordan's bourse fell 0.19 percent on Tuesday after heavy institutional demand on Jordan Housing Bank triggered by a large investor petered out, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index slipped 0.29 points to close at 152.98 points after shares worth 615,026 dinars ($868,680) changed hands. Trade in Housing Bank accounted for nearly half that turnover.

"There was unusual demand on Housing Bank mainly by an institutional portfolio," said Ibrahim Odeh, at Wataniyah Financial Services, citing a better sentiment with signs of a pickup in investor demand on select blue-chips.
Demand on Housing Bank was mainly generated by a single buyer who bought the bulk of 326,000 dinars worth of shares.
The stock fell 0.10 dinars to close at 4.88 dinars after activity generated by the buying petered out, leaving small investors offering smaller quantities at lower prices, brokers said.

Jordan's second largest bank whose commercial banking has overtaken its original real estate lending business, Housing Bank has been in recent days a focus of buying by portfolio investors, brokers said.

Many small investors have been on the sidelines in a wait-and-see mood over the fate of Arab-Israeli peace making. A barometer of sentiment in the Middle East peace process, the market is highly sensitive to regional tension.
An absence of large institutional investors and foreign buyers, who underpinned the market in January and February, has had a dampening effect on trade this month.
Other heavily traded stock on Tuesday were Jordan Cement Factories which rose 0.01 dinars to 3.57 dinars and Bank of Jordan which was unchanged at 2.80 dinars.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 18 to 11, with another 14 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange fell 0.12 percent 80.46 points, 3.52 percent down from the start of the year.
